steps.prompt: Think of a mistake you've made more than once. Why does it keep catching you?

cards.title: Find your danger zones
cards.body: Open My skills (your math progress page). Your danger zones are the skills where you keep losing points: in mocks, checkpoints, problem sets, the daily review and any past papers you've logged. Pick your top three and give each one a redo session from the error log this week.

cards.title: The classic traps
cards.body: Average speed is total distance over total time, not the average of the speeds. Counting from $a$ to $b$ gives $b - a + 1$ numbers. A rise and an equal percent fall don't cancel. "At least one" is easiest as $1 -$ "none". Never divide by something that could be $0$: factor instead.

cards.title: Worked example: average speed
cards.problem: You go $10$ km at $10$ km/h and $10$ km at $30$ km/h. What is your average speed?

steps.text: The times are $1$ hour and $\frac{1}{3}$ of an hour.

try.prompt: How many km do you travel in all?
What is the average speed, in km/h?

cards.title: Past papers count too
cards.body: If you work official AMC 10 papers on your own, mark them and log your answer letters in your past-paper log, with a topic for the problems you can name. Missed topics there show up in your danger zones as well. The log stores letters and topics only, never the problems.

prompts: What are your top three danger zones, and what's your plan for each?
